newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends weaker on MOF Sakakibara remark.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends weaker on MOF Sakakibara remark.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract ended weaker on Thursday after a senior Finance Ministry official remarked that Japan's economy was stronger than the market thought.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Thursday the market view on Japan's economy was too pessimistic and that he believed it was stronger than the market thought.
"The comment came at the right time and provided an opportunity for the market to undergo an adjustment," a brokerage trader said.
A city bank trader said he did not expect the June's slide to last very long, since Sakakibara's comments were unlikely to lead to a change in the market's view of the economy.

Mineko Sasaki-Smith, chief economist CS First Boston said; "(Sakakibara's remark) reflected MOF's desperate attempt to avoid having an additional economic stimulus package when the nation's budget is in bad shape."
As long as Japan has problems with non-performing loans, the economy will not recover robustly, leaving little chance for a credit tightening, Sasaki-Smith said.
The June fell to a low of 99.12 after Sakakibara's remark from the day's high of 99.22.
The next chart resistance lies at 99.09, chartists say.
If it breaches that level, the contract will enter a negative cycle, they added.
In the relatively calmer cash money market, the key three-month certificates of deposit were traded at 0.51 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
The key overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.47 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
Turnover for the June contract was a hefty 13.4985 trillion contracts.
